verification_status_legend.read-via-search-index: Official document text read through a search index excerpt; full document still to be ingested
verification_status_legend.snapshot-stored: Official page downloaded and stored under data/sources/snapshots
verification_status_legend.referenced-not-ingested: Official URL confirmed by an official document; content not yet read

sources.title: CBSE Circular Acad-14/2026 (01.04.2026): Release of CBSE Curriculum for Academic Session 2026-27 for Classes IX-XII
supports: Classes XI-XII curriculum released 1 April 2026, Classes IX-X on 2 April 2026
CBSE implements the NCF-2023 scheme of studies in Class IX from 2026-27
Curriculum documents live at cbseacademic.nic.in/curriculum_2027.html

sources.title: CBSE Curriculum 2026-27 tab (Secondary Part-I Class IX, Secondary Part-I Class X, Senior Secondary Part-II XI-XII)
supports: Subject-wise syllabus PDFs for Classes IX-XII (to ingest in Phase 3)

sources.title: CBSE Circular Acad-33/2026 (15.05.2026): Alignment of Scheme of Studies for Languages in Classes IX and X (2026-27 onwards) with NCF-SE 2023
supports: From 1 July 2026, three languages (R1, R2, R3) compulsory in Class IX, at least two native Indian languages
Class IX students use Class VI R3 textbooks (2026-27 edition) until dedicated R3 books exist
No Class X board exam for R3; R3 assessment school-based and internal
sources.notes: Hindi version read via search excerpt; key clauses corroborated by multiple school circulars quoting Acad-33/2026. English version to ingest.

sources.title: CBSE Circular Acad-49/2026: three-language implementation details by batch (Classes VI to X, 2026-27)
supports: Separate three-language rules for Class X (2026-27), Class IX (2026-27), Classes VII-VIII (2026-27) and Class VI (2026-27) batches
Two of three languages must be Bharatiya Bhashas
sources.notes: Only fragments read. Full batch rules to ingest before Phase 2 placement logic uses them.

sources.title: Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi programme summary (PIB, reproduced by Vikaspedia)
supports: Development domains: physical/motor, cognitive, socio-emotional-ethical, cultural/artistic, communication and early language, literacy and numeracy
At least two hours of pre-school instruction daily at Anganwadi centres
sources.notes: Attach the original PIB release before treating as primary.

sources.title: National Education Policy 2020
sources.issuing_body: Ministry of Education, Government of India
supports: 5+3+3+4 structure: Foundational (ages 3-8), Preparatory (Classes 3-5, ages 8-11), Middle (Classes 6-8, ages 11-14), Secondary (Classes 9-12, ages 14-18)
School examinations in Grades 3, 5 and 8
sources.notes: Structure confirmed via PRS Legislative Research summary (SRC-PRS-NEP-2020-SUMMARY).

sources.title: PRS Legislative Research: National Education Policy 2020 summary
supports: NEP 5+3+3+4 stage bands and ages
Examinations in Grades 3, 5 and 8

sources.title: NIOS Open Basic Education Programme Guideline (revised 01.08.2015)
supports: OBE Level A equivalent to Class 3, Level B to Class 5, Level C to Class 8
OBE recognised by Government of India as equivalent to formal school

sources.title: NIOS SDMIS: About OBE programme
supports: OBE extended in 2000 to children aged 6-14
Target group includes any interested child and children with special needs

sources.title: NIOS Frequently Asked Questions (Secondary and Senior Secondary admission)
supports: Secondary: passed Class VIII and at least 14 years old
Senior Secondary minimum age 15 years
Secondary offers 32 subjects including 17 languages
100% online admission

sources.title: NIOS Senior Secondary scheme of studies (Regional Centre Allahabad page)
supports: Pass requires minimum 5 subjects including one or at most two languages; maximum 7 subjects

Subject codes seen: 301 Hindi, 303 Bengali, 307 Gujarati, 310 Punjabi, 312 Physics, 313 Chemistry, 314 Biology, 319 Business Studies, 328 Psychology, 330 Computer Science, 342 Persian, 373 Physical Education and Yog, 374 Military Studies
sources.notes: Partial table only. Full scheme to ingest from the NIOS prospectus.

sources.title: NIOS Regional Centre Dehradun FAQs (open schooling system, recognition of certificates)
supports: NIOS Secondary and Senior Secondary certificates have the same recognition as certificates of other Boards
NIOS is vested with authority to conduct public examinations at Secondary and Senior Secondary level
Senior Secondary minimum age 15 as on 31 July of the year of admission

sources.title: DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025: commencement dates and children's data provisions (law firm analysis citing the 14 Nov 2025 gazette)
sources.issuing_body: Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co (analysis of MeitY gazette notification)
supports: Three commencement dates: 14 Nov 2025, 14 Nov 2026, 14 May 2027
Substantive obligations including verifiable parental consent apply from 14 May 2027
Certain fiduciaries (including educational institutions) exempt from verifiable consent and the tracking ban for limited purposes
sources.notes: Attach the MeitY gazette (G.S.R.) text before Phase 2 consent flows are finalised.

sources.title: WHO Guidelines on physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep for children under 5 years of age (2019)
supports: Under 1 year: screen time not recommended
1 year: sedentary screen time not recommended; 2 years: no more than 1 hour
3-4 years: no more than 1 hour; less is better
sources.notes: Multiple consistent reports. Attach the WHO publication itself before Phase 2.
